Page 1/9 
Machine Learning (BMI/GEO/WNA) 
Code Assignment U1A1  
Linear Regression 
This is NOT a group Assignment. 
 
10 marks 
Please complete seeing the videos for Week 1-2 before attempting this 
assignment.  
 
Use real estate valuation regression dataset : 
https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/477/real+estate+valuation+data+set  
from the UCI repository, and use google colab to code. 
 
First, download the csv file, and open it in your computer and analyze the 
data. Try to understand what the data is about. Read through the data 
description 
given 
in 
the 
UCI 
website 
as 
well. 
 
Section A 
Answer the following questions [1 mark if you answer all the below 
questions] : 
1. How many samples are there? 
There are 414 samples in the dataset. 
2. How 
many 
input 
variables 
are 
there? 
There are 6 input variables in the dataset. 
X1=the transaction date  
X2=the house age (unit: year) 
X3=the distance to the nearest MRT station (unit: meter)

Page 2/9 
X4=the number of convenience stores in the living circle on foot (integer) 
X5=the geographic coordinate, latitude. (unit: degree) 
X6=the geographic coordinate, longitude. (unit: degree) 
 
3. Which column is the output variable (target outcome)? 
There is one output variable in the dataset : Y= house price of unit 
area. 
4. What does each of the input columns mean ? 
The input values represent various attributes related to real estate 
valuation. 
1. X1=the transaction date - this column represents the date when the transactions 
took place.  
2. X2=the house age (unit: year) - this column represents the age of the house in 
years. 
3. X3=the distance to the nearest MRT station (unit: meter) -this column 
represents the distance from the property to the nearest MRT station.  
4. X4=the number of convenience stores in the living circle on foot (integer) - 
this column represents the count of convenience stores in the living area within 
a particular distance. 
5. X5=the geographic coordinate, latitude. (unit: degree)- this column represents 
the geographical location or coordinate of the property in terms of its north-
south position, measured in degrees. 
6. X6=the geographic coordinate, longitude. (unit: degree) - this column 
represents the geographical coordinate of the property in terms of its east-west 
position, 
measured 
in 
degrees.  
 
Section B 
For each of the questions below, you need to put in the screenshot of the 
code and its output. You could use the sample google colab file that is 
provided with this assignment.

Page 3/9 
1. Understanding the dataset [4 marks] 
There are many input variables in this dataset. Use only X1 to X4 as input 
variables, and y as the output variable. 
Using the scatter plots between each of the input features (X1-X4) and the 
output (Y), which input variable, do you think, is better in predicting 
the output / target variable ? 
1. Input variable X1 
 
 
2. Input variable X2

Page 6/9 
 
 
 
 
 
The input variable house age and distance to the nearest MRT station 
will be a better input variable in predicting the output variable as both 
have a direct linear proportion to each other. House age indicates the 
structural conditions and design model of a house which directly 
affects the price of house. 
 
2. Write code to find out how many samples are there in total in this 
dataset? [1 mark]

Page 7/9 
 
 
 
3. What is the train test split ratio that you have chosen ? [1 Mark] 
 
The train-test ratio is 75-25%. 
 
4. Evaluate the linear regression model by computing the MAE, MSE and 
Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) . 
(for MAPE - pls refer to the sample here - https://scikit-
learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.mean_absolute_perce
ntage_error.html)  
[3 marks]

Page 8/9 
 
 
5. What are the 3 new things that you learned after you completed this 
assignment ? 
1. MAPE- mean absolute percentage error  
2. MAE 
3. MSE
